solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some backward Neanderthal biker that's turned to praying

indicators.note: the run found inside the words is to be read from right to left
only some of the letters of the next words are wanted, a run lying inside them

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A caveman motorcyclist has had a change of heart and taken up prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, neanderTHAL BIKer gives KIBLAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiblah is the direction of Mecca, which Muslims face when they pray, so it is what one turns towards for prayer.

clue.text: Iron a coat found among gear with energy

indicators.note: something found among other things sits in the middle of them

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear
a mac is a raincoat
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Instructions for pressing a coat that turns up in a pile of equipment, done energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like a verb for pressing the coat; it is the noun, a metal. A MAC sits inside KIT, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamacite is a nickel-poor alloy of metallic iron found chiefly in meteorites.

clue.text: Shrub to become perky after removal of root

indicators.note: in a down entry the root is the bottom letter, so the last letter is taken away

parts.note: to buck up is to cheer up and grow lively

explanation.surface: A gardener's note on a plant that revives once its root is cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the root is the foot of the word, so the final P of BUCK UP goes, leaving BUCKU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucku, also spelt buchu, is a South African shrub whose leaves are used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: American means to cut commercials from radio

indicators.note: what comes over the radio is heard, not seen, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: ads are advertisements

explanation.surface: An American way of trimming the adverts out of a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests censoring commercials, but 'American means to cut' is the definition: the US spelling of a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adz, the American spelling of adze, is a cutting tool with a blade set at right angles to its handle.

clue.text: Spartan character, coldness, about old, old Jack: what Daisy would give for a laugh!

definitions.text: what Daisy would give for a laugh

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes about, that is around, the following letters

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Sparta
O is the abbreviation for old, twice
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
ice is coldness

explanation.surface: A jumble of Greek letters, chill and old card-players, ending with a joke about a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy is a stock name for a cow, and 'for a laugh' marks the answer as jokey slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Moo-juice is humorous slang for milk, which is what a cow called Daisy would produce.

clue.text: Fern, abnormally large and dull, couple in the end pruned

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, and a couple at the end means the last two letters go

parts.note: OS stands for outsize
mundane means dull and ordinary

explanation.surface: A gardener complains of an overgrown, boring fern, two ends of which have been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is outsize, as on clothing labels; MUNDANE loses its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmunda is the genus of royal ferns, large ferns of wet ground.

clue.text: Good medium's supernatural power, making second judge check one false statement

indicators.note: the second of two like letters is made into something else, replaced by what follows

parts.note: juju is magic power attributed to a charm or fetish
J is the abbreviation for judge; it is the second J that goes
to stem is to check or stop a flow
I is the Roman numeral one
a lie is an untrue statement

explanation.surface: A psychic medium's powers turn out to rest on a fraudulent judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good medium' looks like a spiritualist; it is the definition. In JUJU the second J is swapped for STEM, I and LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Juste milieu is French for the happy mean, the sensible middle course between extremes.

clue.text: Camise? 14 for mending: will I bring pins and needles?

definitions.text: will I bring pins and needles

indicators.note: something put in for mending is reworked, so these letters are rebuilt

parts.note: a camise is a loose shirt or tunic
the answer to 14 across

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a shirt sent for repair will come back full of pins and needles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pins and needles' suggests sewing a shirt, but here it is the tingling of poor circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischaemia is a restricted blood supply to part of the body, one of whose symptoms is tingling numbness.

clue.text: What's to be mostly seen round Rome with no sleeves?

definitions.text: What's to be mostly seen round Rome with no sleeves?

indicators.note: the shortened verb goes round, enclosing, the city's core
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to exist is to be

indicators.note: the sleeves are the outer edges of the word, which are stripped off

parts.note: the inner letters of the city's name

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a person might be wearing around ancient Rome without sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: EXIS(t) wraps round (r)OM(e). The whole clue also defines: a sleeveless garment of the classical world.
explanation.definitionFit: The exomis was a short tunic of ancient Greece and Rome, fastened over one shoulder and leaving the arms bare.

clue.text: Kabul resident perhaps has right to replace fine fibre

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: Kabul is the capital of Afghanistan
R is the abbreviation for right
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An Afghan citizen has the right to swap good thread for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine fibre' reads as one phrase, but fine is F, swapped out for R in AFGHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arghan is the strong fibre obtained from a tropical American plant related to the pineapple.

clue.text: Prayer books from church in Hampton Court feature briefly round border

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is placed in the shortened garden feature
briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace near London has a famous hedge maze
CH is the abbreviation for church
a round shape is an O
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Prayer books found in the chapel at Hampton Court, the royal palace near London, beside its famous maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hampton Court feature' could be many things; the hedge maze is the one everyone knows, cut short here.
explanation.definitionFit: Machzorim, plural of machzor, are Jewish prayer books containing the liturgy for festivals and holy days.

clue.text: Passable firm's turned around, becoming first rate

indicators.note: turning around faces the letters the other way, so they read from right to left

parts.note: OK means acceptable, passable
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm, plus S

explanation.surface: A mediocre company has a turnaround and becomes excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: OK and CO'S together, read backwards, give SOCKO.
explanation.definitionFit: Socko is American slang for impressive or excellent, a knockout success.

clue.text: Peanuts from US or China drop in copper plate finally

indicators.note: the word for the drop is placed in among the letters that follow

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, so a china is a chum
a copper is a police constable, a PC
the drop is the gallows, so to drop someone is to hang them

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A trader compares the price of nuts from America and China, dropped into a copper dish.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is rhyming slang for mate. 'Peanuts' is not nuts at all but a trifling sum of money, and the drop is the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Chump change is American slang for a paltry amount of money, the same idea as the British peanuts.

clue.text: First victim from railway engine in section overturned

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run the opposite way up the down light
the engine word is placed in the section word

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway
a motor is an engine
a part is a section

explanation.surface: An accident report: the first casualty came from a train engine that overturned in a section of line.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the railway and engine words are overturned here; the section word stays the right way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A protomartyr is the first martyr of a cause, chiefly St Stephen, the first Christian killed for his faith.

clue.text: Off and on, yacht is bringing tuna

indicators.note: off then on again in turn means every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of these words

explanation.surface: An intermittent yacht trip lands a tuna.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of yAcHt Is are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahi is the Hawaiian name for yellowfin or bigeye tuna, common on menus.

clue.text: Examine love, performing a bit of Henry VIII

parts.note: to test is to examine
love is nil, zero in tennis, an O
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: An actor auditions for a love scene playing a small part in a Henry VIII drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of Henry VIII' sounds like a bit part in the play; it is a coin of his reign.
explanation.definitionFit: The testoon was a silver shilling coin first struck under Henry VIII, so a piece of his money.

clue.text: Porter, maybe, within seconds to bring up mineral

indicators.note: the porter is placed within the letters that follow

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
Cole Porter was the American songwriter
to cite is to bring up or mention

explanation.surface: A railway porter is asked to carry a heavy rock up in seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a luggage carrier; it is Cole Porter, sitting inside S and CITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scolecite is a white zeolite mineral, a hydrated calcium aluminium silicate forming needle-like crystals.

clue.text: Plant's charm, with tips pruned

indicators.note: pruning the tips cuts off both ends, the first and last letters

parts.note: a talisman is a lucky charm

explanation.surface: A gardener's view of a plant's appeal once its shoots have been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant's' reads as possessive, but the 's is plant is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Alisma is the water-plantain genus, marsh plants with small white or pink flowers.

clue.text: Harp on about husband, awful rascal!

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so these letters are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
C is circa, about
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife keeps nagging about her terrible rogue of a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harp on' looks like a phrase meaning nag; harp is the definition and on merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarsach is the old Celtic harp of Scotland and Ireland, strung with wire.

clue.text: American fly-by-night books in place of Douglas and Henry

parts.note: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, IOM
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An untrustworthy American has swapped some books for those of a man called Douglas and another called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly-by-night' sounds like a shady person; here it is literally something that flies by night.
explanation.definitionFit: The io moth is a large North American moth, flying at night, with eyespots on its hindwings.

clue.text: Familiar greeting to composer descending on one's barbecue

indicators.note: in a down light coming down onto something means sitting on top of it

parts.note: hi is a casual hello
J S Bach, the German composer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cheery hello to a composer who drops in on someone's cookout.
explanation.definitionFit: A hibachi is a small Japanese charcoal brazier, used as a portable grill for cooking food outdoors.

clue.text: Wind belt up — one metre length — around hollow area

indicators.note: the letters before go around the emptied word

parts.note: belt up is British slang for be quiet, and sh calls for silence
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for metre

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Instructions for a gust: buckle up, then go a metre around an empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt up' looks like fastening a seat belt; it is British slang for shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: The shimaal, or shamal, is a hot dry north-westerly wind blowing over Iraq and the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Muslim's honorary title for one self-made, on the up

parts.note: say means for example, for one

indicators.note: going up a down light means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, made oneself

explanation.surface: A self-made man on the rise is honoured with a title.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'on the up' reverses only the self-made part, which sits below the example word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayyid is an honorific given to Muslims descended from the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Public notice UK spies holding short interrogation

indicators.note: the spies hold the questioning, enclosing it within them

parts.note: SIS is the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's MI6

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to quiz is to interrogate

explanation.surface: A news notice that British spies are detaining someone for a brief questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Latin for 'if anyone', the opening words of such a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A si quis is a notice posted in a parish church inviting objections before a candidate is ordained.

clue.text: You might catch spotted fish

indicators.note: catching something can mean hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: eyed means looked at, spotted

explanation.surface: An angler's tip: a fish with spots is one you might land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted fish' reads as a fish with markings; spotted is a separate word meaning seen, and catch means hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater fish of the carp family, also called the orfe.

clue.text: A mix of beer and bubbly for brother not up to much?

indicators.note: a mix of things stirs them together, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cocktail of beer and champagne served to a monk who is not much use.
explanation.walkthrough: Brother here is a monk, and a lazy one fits a surface about drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey-lubber was an idle, well-fed monk, an old term of contempt for a useless brother of a religious house.

clue.text: Sailor reared collection of animals for chops

indicators.note: rearing up in a down light means rising, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
a zoo is a collection of animals

explanation.surface: A seaman raised a menagerie destined for the butcher's chops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chops' suggests cuts of meat; it is the slang for the mouth or jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Bazoo is American slang for the mouth, and chops is slang for the jaws or mouth.

clue.text: Christian attending college, having changed order

indicators.note: the two pieces are set down in the opposite order to that in which they first come

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
at means attending, as in at school

explanation.surface: A believer goes to college and comes away with a new religious allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: Attending college is AT UNI; swapping the two words gives UNIAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uniat is a member of an Eastern Christian church in communion with Rome but keeping its own rites.

clue.text: Archie played retro musical style with no initial clarity

indicators.note: the name is played with, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the letters run the other way
the first letter of the musical style is lost

parts.note: jazz is a style of music

explanation.surface: A musician named Archie played old-fashioned jazz but lacked clarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' looks like it describes the music; it signals reversal of (j)AZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiarezza is Italian for clearness, used of purity and clarity in musical performance.

clue.text: Delivered, but not initially from the pen of Sir Walter Scott?

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: delivered from harm means set free

explanation.surface: A letter delivered that was perhaps not penned by the novelist Walter Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the pen of' usually means written by; here pen is an enclosure, in a Scots word Scott used.
explanation.definitionFit: Ree is a Scots word for an enclosure or sheepfold, found in Scott's novels, so a pen in his vocabulary.

clue.text: Go around stores to pick up safety device

indicators.note: something that stores another holds it inside

parts.note: to spin is to go around
to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone tours the shops to collect a piece of safety equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stores' looks like shops; it is a verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shear pin is a pin designed to break under excessive load, protecting machinery from damage.

clue.text: Before the first hour, rushed unknown quantity back

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hour
tore means rushed
x, y and z stand for unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone dashed back before the first hour struck, to an uncertain outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before the first hour' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeroth means coming before the first in a series, as in the zeroth law of thermodynamics.
